question: How many vehicles will the Texas DMV automated-vehicle registry have listed for Tesla on December 29, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Registry count ~1,282 around Nov 8, 2026 (1,204 on Nov 1; 803 on Oct 17; 420 on Sep 2). Growth has run 11-22/day recently, in lumpy batches; about 49-50 days remain to Dec 29. Continuing at a blended ~14/day gives roughly 1,990. Upside: Cybercab ramp, new Texas cities (Fort Worth, San Antonio), year-end push. Downside: holiday slowdown, plateau after passing Waymo, deregistrations. No matching human market; Polymarket only has Tesla Q4 delivery-count markets (different quantity, not usable as an anchor).
calls.dossier:
- Resolves off the VIN count on TxDMV TxMCCS page for Tesla Robotaxi, LLC automated motor vehicles, accessed on/after Dec 29, 2026. Not deliveries or active fleet.
- Event window: point-in-time snapshot on/after 2026-12-29; as of 2026-11-10 ~49 days remain from the last known datapoint.
- Registry opened May 2026 with Tesla at 42 vehicles (Drive Tesla / CNBC, May 28 2026).
- ~Sep 2 2026: 420 vehicles (TeslaNorth).
- Sep 18 2026: 58 Cybercabs registered (TeslaNorth).
- Oct 17 2026: 803 (454 Model Y + 349 Cybercab) (search snippet of tracker).
- Late Oct: 811 (+8 Model Y), then 970 -> 1,051 (+81 Cybercab) (RobotaxiTracker X posts).
- Nov 1 2026: 1,204 (631 Model Y, 573 Cybercab), +124 Model Y batch; Waymo 1,259, Avride 344, Zoox 63 (TeslaNorth Nov 1).
- ~Nov 7-9 2026: 1,282 (+38 Model Y from 1,244); Waymo 1,285 (phil beisel X; Drive Tesla).
- Observed rates: ~13/day averaged Sep2-Nov8; ~22/day Oct17-Nov1; ~11/day Nov1-Nov8. Additions arrive in batches of 8-124.
- Expansion: Fort Worth launch early Nov, San Antonio Nov 9 (8 cities total) (TeslaOracle). Cybercab production ramping.
- Counter-evidence: Electrek Sep 22 reported active Austin fleet much smaller than registry; holiday period may slow additions; possible removals were not observed in the data found.
- Searched but not found: exact count after Nov 9; any deregistration events; official Tesla year-end Texas target. No human market on this registry count (Polymarket only Q4 deliveries).
calls.reference_class: Tesla's own Texas AV-registry growth trajectory, Sep-Nov 2026, extrapolated over a 50-day window

calls.reasoning: Registry at 1,282 on Nov 9 2026 (631 Model Y + ~600 Cybercab, rising from ~420 on Sep 2, 803 Oct 17, 970 Oct 24, 1204 Nov 1). Linear continuation of the ~13/day Sep-Nov average gives ~1,920 on Dec 29; the recent 2-week rate (~18/day) gives ~2,160. Additions are lumpy batches; the Cybercab ramp and Texas city launches (Fort Worth, San Antonio) argue for acceleration, while holidays and possible deregistrations argue for a slowdown. No human market prices this registry count; the Polymarket delivery markets are a different contract and weren't used.

calls.reasoning: Tesla Robotaxi LLC count on the TxDMV registry rose from 476 (Sep 22) to 739 (Oct 9), 970 (Oct 24), 1,080 (Oct 28), 1,204 (Nov 1) and 1,282 (Nov 9). Since late Oct essentially all additions are Cybercabs; Model Y has been flat at 507. Pace was about 17.5/day over Oct 9-Nov 9 and about 10/day over the last 8 days, with lumpy batches. Projecting 49 days gives about 1,770 at 10/day and about 2,110 at 17/day; holiday or production slowdown is the downside, a production ramp or Dallas launch the upside. No human market on this registry count was found; the Polymarket Q4 delivery markets are a different contract and were not used.
calls.dossier:
- Resolves off the count of VINs listed under Tesla Robotaxi, LLC on the TxDMV automated motor vehicle database (txmccs.txdmv.gov), as accessed on or after 2026-12-29. It does not resolve off active fleet size; registered VINs are not cars carrying riders (Electrek Sep 22 reported about 8 active vehicles in Austin).
- Event window: point-in-time count on 2026-12-29. As of Now (2026-11-10), 49 days remain; window is a snapshot, not cumulative.
- Sep 22, 2026: 476 VINs (409 Model Y, 67 Cybercab) (Electrek/search snippet).
- Cybercabs first appeared Aug 31, 2026 (45). Sep 23: 69 Cybercabs; Sep 28: 126; Oct 8: 169 Cybercabs, 589 total (evwire).
- Oct 9: +150 Cybercabs in one batch -> 739 total (319 CC / 420 MY) (evwire, teslanorth).
- Oct 24 tracker baseline: 507 MY + 463 CC = 970 (derekbeau1 GitHub tracker). One report cited 811 (449 CC/362 MY) on Oct 21 — inconsistent.
- Oct 27: 1,051 (544 CC/507 MY); Oct 28: 1,080 (573 CC/507 MY) (teslanorth, driveteslacanada).
- Nov 1: 1,204; Nov 9: 1,282, 3 behind Waymo's 1,285 on the same registry (driveteslacanada).
- Model Y count flat at 507 since about Oct 24; growth is Cybercab-driven. Additions are lumpy (single-day batches of 11, 29, 81, 150).
- Rates: Oct 9->Nov 9 about 17.5/day; Oct 24->Nov 1 about 29/day; Nov 1->Nov 9 about 10/day. Sep 22->Oct 8 about 7/day.
- Arithmetic: 1,282 + 49 x {5, 10, 17, 25} = {1,527, 1,772, 2,115, 2,507}.
- Upside candidates: Cybercab production ramp at Giga Texas; Dallas/Houston launches (Dallas Cybercab launch reported targeted for Nov 2026); renewed Model Y registrations. Downside candidates: holiday slowdown, production bottlenecks, deregistrations/removals (tracker logs removals), registry outage.
- Searched for but not found: live current count (tracker pages render via JS), Tesla guidance on Cybercab deployment numbers for end of 2026, any prediction market on this registry count (none found).
calls.reference_class: Linear extrapolation of the Tesla TxDMV automated vehicle registry growth rate over the Sep-Nov 2026 trailing windows

calls.reconciliation: Run 3's 'Model Y flat at 507' conflicts with Runs 1-2, which report a +124 MY batch near Oct 31 (631 MY / 573 CC) and +38 MY near Nov 9. The arithmetic only works if Model Y kept growing, so both vehicle types are still being added, which supports a slightly higher central rate than Run 3's. The Oct 17/21 count conflict (803 vs 811) can't be settled from the dossiers and doesn't affect the trend. Removals are possible but small. The central-rate question is judgment: I take ~13-14/day, median ~1,950, with a right skew for the production ramp and city launches. Dispersion is in line with the runs.
